newsitem.title: UK: BA expects to run 95 percent of flights Monday.
newsitem.headline: BA expects to run 95 percent of flights Monday.

text.p: British Airways Plc said Friday it anticipated 95 percent of its flights worldwide would operate as of Monday as staff continued to trickle back to work after last week's strike by flight attendants.

A BA spokesman said about 150 flight attendants a day were returning from sick leave since the strike ended last Friday, but 1,200 were still out sick -- twice the number normally expected for this time of year.
Service out of London's Gatwick airport is already back to normal, and the airline said it planned to operate all but a handful of flights from London's Heathrow airport.

The airline and the cabin crew union -- representing nearly 9,000 members -- have agreed to reopen talks in the dispute over pay, after the union offered to make new proposals on how to find the 42 million pounds ($70 million) of savings sought by management from a new pay structure.
However, BA said the flight attendants' union, part of the Transport and General Workers Union (T&G), had not yet submitted its proposals on making the savings.
A union spokeswoman confirmed the union was still drafting them and said the documents could be sent to BA's management "at some point next week."
T&G representative Andrew Murray said Wednesday that once BA received its proposals, negotiations would begin. Talks are expected to take two to three weeks.
BA said Tuesday the strike had already cost the company "tens of millions of pounds" as well as lost bookings for the future and urged the union to adopt a "constructive approach."
